subject: Azure Private Plan — entitlement & invoice routing playbook
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@medvantage.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medvantage.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify entitlements and invoice routing for Azure Private Plan

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the briefing last week. Procurement has reviewed the proposed Private Plan terms and we have two items blocking PO issuance:

1) Entitlement mapping — we need a clear exhibit that maps which customer seats/entitlements are provisioned in Azure vs on Redwood billing. The security team is asking for an auditable entitlements exhibit we can attach to the PO.

2) Invoice routing for co-sell — our finance team requires the invoice flow diagram showing when Microsoft versus MedVantage receives billings, how tax is handled, and who issues credits for overage adjustments.

Can you send a short playbook or example exhibit you’ve used for other private plan customers? If possible, include any language you recommend for the PO and a one-page invoice flow graphic.

Thanks,
Lisa Park
Director, Procurement
MedVantage Health

[This message has an attachment: invoice_requirements_111.pdf]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@medvantage.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify entitlements and invoice routing for Azure Private Plan

Hi Lisa —

Appreciate the clear list. I’m attaching a short playbook and a sample entitlement exhibit we’ve used with other Azure private plan customers. High level notes below:

- Entitlement exhibit: We map SKU-level entitlements to Azure Private Plan resource IDs and include a version field (model-version + date) so both parties can audit provisioning changes. The attached doc (redwood-privatesku-entitlement-exhibit.docx) is editable for your legal.
- Invoice flow: For co-sell the commercial model we recommended is: Redwood invoices customer for usage (single bill) while Microsoft issues a merchant settlement to Redwood on co-sell terms. For MedVantage customers that want Microsoft invoicing first, we can support an MSP routing but it requires an additional revenue-split exhibit and an explicit billing contact. See the diagram (invoice_flow_diagram.png).
- PO language: We suggest two clauses: (1) Entitlement exhibit incorporated by ref; (2) Invoice routing and crediting mechanism described with a 30-day dispute window.

Irene is looped in for any legal redlines; Marissa will help with the co-sell revenue exhibit if you want a draft.

Attachments: redwood-privatesku-entitlement-exhibit.docx, invoice_flow_diagram.png, MedVantage_AMS_SOW_draft.pdf

Next steps: If this looks good I can share a tracked-change exhibit for your counsel and draft a one-page PO insert you can attach to your purchase order.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: redwood-privatesku-entitlement-exhibit.docx (editable), invoice_flow_diagram.png (PNG, 1 page), MedVantage_AMS_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW, draft)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Clarify entitlements and invoice routing for Azure Private Plan

Forwarding Lisa’s ask and Nikhil’s playbook. Quick notes from commercial:

- For customers in our co-sell pipeline we usually accept the Entitlement Exhibit as an appendix to the PO and require monthly meter reports from Azure to reconcile usage. That keeps Microsoft satisfied and prevents double-billing.
- For invoice routing, the majority prefer Redwood-led billing with a merchant settlement from MS — reduces accounts payable complexity for them. If MedVantage insists on MS billing, we need a 6-month lookback clause for credits and a retained evidence clause to reconcile disputes.

Irene — can you mark up the entitlement exhibit with any language we should explicitly require (audit windows, versioning, data retention for monthly meter files)? I’d like to keep this tight so procurement can sign.

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Sales — Cloud Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify entitlements and invoice routing for Azure Private Plan

Lisa / Marissa / Nikhil —

Thanks for the materials. I reviewed the exhibit and propose the following changes (summary):

1) Audit & versioning: Add explicit audit clause in the entitlement exhibit: Redwood to provide monthly entitlement export in CSV within 5 business days of month-end; both parties retain copies for 12 months for dispute resolution.
2) PO incorporation: Entitlement Exhibit must be incorporated by reference in the PO; any changes require a written, signed amendment.
3) Credits & disputes: 30-day dispute window after invoice issuance; if a reconciliation results in a credit, Redwood will issue a credit memo applied to the next invoice unless parties agree otherwise.

I attached a tracked-change version of the exhibit and a one-page PO insert (attached) for your legal to attach. Marissa — for the MS invoicing path, we should add the 6-month lookback only if Redwood is not the invoicing entity.

Please confirm and we’ll produce a marked-up doc for your counsel.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-privatesku-entitlement-exhibit_marked.docx, PO_insertion_onepager.pdf
